The browser submits a `CreateIssueInput` to `createIssueAction`, which validates it, resolves the signed-in member as an `Actor`, checks permission and the project’s plan quota, and calls the issue service. The service repeats its own scope, project, permission and quota checks before inserting the issue. After the insert, it publishes `issue.created`; registered listeners update activity, search, usage and webhook delivery records before the action returns.

Before submission, the new-issue page in [page.tsx](</private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/new/page.tsx>) calls `loadProjectContext` to resolve the tenant, actor and project. It checks `can(actor, "issue:create", ...)` and returns a 404 if denied. It also calls `getPlanLimits` and `listIssues` with `includeArchived: true`; if the project is full, it renders the quota message instead of the form. Otherwise it loads members and labels and passes `createIssueAction` to `IssueForm`. The organization’s stored default status is checked against `issueStatusSchema`, falling back to `backlog`.

[IssueForm](</private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/components/domain/issue/issue-form.tsx>) uses React Hook Form and `zodResolver(createIssueSchema)`. On submit, `handleSubmit` validates before calling `useFormAction`’s `submit`, which invokes the Server Action and tracks pending and error state. The schema in [src/schemas/issue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/schemas/issue.ts) defines `CreateIssueInput`: IDs must have the branded ULID format, the title is 3–200 characters, description is at most 20,000, estimate is a nullable integer from 0 to 100, due date is a nullable ISO timestamp, and there can be at most 20 labels. It also constrains status and priority and supplies defaults for optional values.

`createIssueAction(raw: unknown): Promise<ActionResult<Issue>>` in [src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts) delegates to a function made by `withAction` in [src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts). The wrapper first runs `createIssueSchema.safeParse` again on the server. If it succeeds, `resolveActorFor` uses the parsed `orgId` and calls `requireActorFor`. That reads the session cookie through `getSessionPrincipal`, resolves and checks the session expiry, finds the organization, and calls `resolveActorForOrg`. The latter requires an active membership, constructs the `Actor` with user, organization and role, checks its scope, and updates the member’s last-seen time. These functions live in [src/lib/actor.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/lib/actor.ts), [src/lib/session.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/lib/session.ts) and [src/server/services/session-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/services/session-service.ts).

The action handler then calls `can` for `issue:create` using a provisional issue resource. In [src/lib/permissions.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/lib/permissions.ts), the decision checks tenant equality first, then a platform-staff bypass, then the role matrix. Creating an issue requires at least the `member` role; issue ownership does not grant this action. Next, `assertProjectHasRoom` gets the organization summary and its `issuesPerProject` limit, then calls `listIssues` for the project with archived issues included. At or above the limit it throws `PlanLimitError`.

[createIssue]( /private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/services/issue-service.ts) applies another set of gates: `assertOrgScope`; a tenant-scoped `findProjectById` and `requireFound`; `assertNotArchived` on the project; and `assertCan` for `issue:create` on the project resource. It loads the organization and uses `countIssues` plus `wouldExceedLimit` for the service-level quota check. There is a distinction between these checks: the action includes archived issues, while `countIssues` is called with its default scope and counts live issues. The action’s archived-inclusive check therefore governs this browser path.

Once those checks pass, `nextIssueNumber` in [src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts) finds the maximum number for that organization and project, including archived rows, and adds one. `insertIssue` generates an ID and inserts into the Drizzle `issues` table defined in [src/server/db/schema/issues.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/db/schema/issues.ts). It stores the submitted fields, the actor’s user ID as author, the allocated number and timestamps; `startedAt` and `completedAt` start as null. Selected labels are inserted separately into `issue_labels`, and `toIssue` maps the returned `IssueRow` and label IDs into the domain `Issue` type.

The code does not wrap the quota check, number allocation, issue insert and label inserts in one transaction. The database has a unique index on project and issue number, but concurrent submissions can race, and a failure during label insertion can occur after the issue row has been inserted. The create path also validates the *format* of assignee, parent and label IDs; it does not perform separate existence or tenant checks on those references in `createIssue` or `insertIssue`.

After `insertIssue` returns, `createIssue` awaits `emit("issue.created", ...)`. The payload is the `TaskflowEventMap["issue.created"]` type from [src/types/event.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/types/event.ts): an `EventEnvelope` containing organization, actor and occurrence time, plus issue and project IDs, title, assignee and priority. In the Node runtime, [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/instrumentation.ts) registers the listeners through [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/services/event-registry.ts). The bus runs subscribers concurrently and waits for them to settle; a subscriber failure is reported to error sinks and does not fail the emit or its siblings.

For this event, the registered consequences are:

- `registerActivityListeners` in [activity-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/services/activity-service.ts) calls `record` to insert an `issue.created` activity row with the actor, issue, project, title and priority.
- `registerSearchListeners` in [search-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/services/search-service.ts) re-reads the issue and calls `indexIssue`, which upserts a search document containing its title and description.
- `registerUsageListeners` in [usage-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/services/usage-service.ts) increments the organization’s cached `issuesUsed` counter.
- `registerWebhookListeners` in [webhook-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/services/webhook-service.ts) creates pending delivery rows for enabled organization endpoints subscribed to `issue.created`. The scheduled [webhook delivery job](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/server/jobs/webhook-delivery-job.ts) later checks plan and flag eligibility, signs and logs the payload, and marks it delivered; this implementation does not make an outbound HTTP request.

Creating an issue with an assignee does not itself emit `issue.assigned`, so the notification service’s assignment listener does not run on this path.

Finally, the action invalidates the organization, project and new-issue cache tags; `withAction` also invalidates the static `issues` tag, using the minutes profile. The wrapper returns a timestamped `ActionResult<Issue>`. On success, `useFormAction` clears its error and `IssueForm` resets; it does not navigate. On failure, the wrapper passes the error through `toActionResult` and the form displays the returned message. One detail of the current implementation is that [src/lib/errors.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/a6f8e1d9-981a-4d82-8a39-cca8f33ffc6c/src/lib/errors.ts) explicitly maps Zod and several domain errors, but not the action-specific `ForbiddenActionError` or `PlanLimitError`, so those fall through to `internal_error` despite carrying their own codes.
